title: Value equation — short research note
text: An offer becomes more attractive when the buyer wants the outcome and believes success is plausible. Reducing the wait for results and the work demanded of the buyer also raises perceived value. This suggests examining both the desired result and the friction of achieving it, rather than treating a lower price as the only improvement.

title: Bonuses — short research note
text: Useful bonuses address obstacles a customer expects to face. A practical tool or checklist can remove work more directly than another course to watch. When choosing a bonus, consider whether it makes the customer's path easier and faster instead of merely increasing the amount of material delivered.

title: Specific knowledge — short research note
text: Distinctive expertise can grow from sustained curiosity and individual interests. Combining that expertise with responsibility for outcomes and ways to amplify output creates a stronger economic position. The emphasis is on capabilities that distinguish a person rather than generic training that makes workers interchangeable.
attribution: Original brief paraphrase prepared for this demo from Naval's published discussion; not a quotation or full transcript.

title: Product and media — short research note
text: Software and published media can reach additional people without repeating the original work for each recipient. Unlike hiring workers or raising investment, writing code or publishing content does not first require another person to grant resources. A small team can combine product, media and capital to amplify its output.

title: Repeatable hooks — short research note
text: Kallaway presents hooks as a central component of short-form storytelling. He argues that creators benefit from a repeatable way of designing openings instead of relying on inconsistent inspiration. His described approach draws on experiments and analysis of creators across educational and entertainment categories.
attribution: Original brief paraphrase prepared for this demo from Kane Kallaway's newsletter; not a quotation or full transcript.

title: Hook psychology — short research note
text: The workshop description includes studying viewer psychology as part of improving video hooks. The focus is on understanding the audience's response to an opening. This brief source note does not contain the full workshop method or justify promises of a particular view count.
